about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Brazil's corn-ethanol build-out is gaining a new buyer, with Petrobras seeking more supply deals, which supports Brazilian domestic corn use and could slow its export surplus over time. Near term, Dec delivery and a finished US harvest keep the tone heavy; rail-merger worries are a logistics footnote.
events: Petrobras to seek more corn ethanol deals after Neomille (Reuters)
Corn growers raise concerns over rail merger (Brownfield)
Corn and beans tick higher overnight as dollar pauses (Pro Farmer)

soybeans.fundamental: Jan reached a November high on Tuesday on reports of a new US-China deal, then eased to about 1,226 overnight, back at the 1,225 pivot. Strong meal-led crush demand is the firm underpinning; confirmed Chinese purchases are still needed to hold a break above 1,240.
events: Soybeans hit November highs on China deal talk (AgroLatam, AgWeb)
Jan ~1,226 overnight, down ~0.7% (CBOT/Yahoo Finance)
Soybeans firm as the real rebounds (American Ag Network)

meal.fundamental: Meal holds near 351 Jan after leading the complex; strong meal demand is keeping crush running hard even as soyoil slides, so meal carries the crush margin. No new Argentine supply news.
events: Strong meal demand boosts crush (Bloomberg)
Soybeans rally as meal leads (Barchart)

oil.fundamental: Soyoil hit a nine-month low (Jan ~57.7, -1.1%) as heavy crush for meal adds oil supply. China's soyoil export surge is cooling as India switches to palm, which trims competition for US export demand only slightly; nothing new on US biofuel policy.
events: Soyoil at nine-month low as meal demand drives crush (Bloomberg)
China soyoil export boom cools as India turns to palm (Bloomberg)

wheat.fundamental: Chicago Mar slipped about 1% to ~589 as early Black Sea support faded and US winter wheat ratings keep improving; Barchart's wrap also flags lagging US export pace in the wider grain complex.
events: Wheat slips into Thanksgiving (Barchart)
Chicago wheat dips on firmer dollar (Investing.com)
Black Sea tensions lift wheat early (Fastmarkets)

kc.fundamental: KC Mar eased about 0.9% to ~632, following Chicago lower; better Plains crop ratings keep 2027 HRW supply risk low.
events: Wheat slips into Thanksgiving (Barchart)
Winter wheat ratings up a third week (AgroLatam)

cotton.fundamental: Mar is steady near 81.5-81.7 after Tuesday's gain, which Barchart tied mostly to outside markets rather than fresh cotton demand. Old-crop Mar/May still rests on Texas Plains crop losses; Dec delivery and high-grade certificated stocks remain a risk for longs, so the firmness is not yet a demand signal.
events: Cotton closes Tuesday higher on outside-market help (Barchart)
Mar ~81.5 in early trade, little changed (ICE/Yahoo Finance)
Texas Plains drought trims dryland yields (Farm Progress)

hogs.fundamental: Dec hogs made new lows (~51.8) as weak pork demand and a pre-holiday cutout sale weigh; large Dec open interest into expiry keeps liquidation pressure on, with the index still above Dec.
events: Lean hogs fall to new lows on weak pork demand (The Pig Site)
Hogs close lower as cutout goes on pre-Thanksgiving sale (Barchart)
Fewer hogs slaughtered, less pork sold (National Hog Farmer)

cattle.fundamental: Live cattle were mixed (Dec ~226) while the market waits for direct cash trade; tight supply after the friendly Cattle on Feed remains the core. Screwworm and the closed Mexican border stay the main two-sided risk.
events: Cattle futures mixed waiting on direct trade (Brownfield)
Live cattle rally on bullish COF and higher cash (AgWeb, ADMIS)
US screwworm cases surge (Reuters)

feeders.fundamental: Lower placements and the closed Mexican border keep feeder supply tight, but cheaper corn helps feedlot demand; screwworm spread is the key tail risk for both supply and sentiment.
events: Bullish COF lifts cattle complex (Barchart, ADMIS)
Screwworm cases surge, border cattle remain on hold (Reuters, RFD-TV)
USDA announces new tools for beef industry (Michigan Farm News)

class3.fundamental: Dec Class III bounced about 1.6% to ~17.2 with CME block cheese firmer, but milk output growth near 2% y/y still caps cheese; a slowing pizza market is a demand watch point.
events: Class III Dec ~17.2, cheese +1.6% (Yahoo Finance/CME)
Is a slowing pizza market bad news for dairy? (Dairy Herd)

class4.fundamental: Spot nonfat dry milk dropped 7 cents at CME, a soft signal for powder demand; Class IV futures barely moved, so the cash weakness has yet to feed through.
events: Nonfat dry milk drops 7 cents at CME (Brownfield)
Class IV Mar ~19.3, little changed (Yahoo Finance/CME)

palm.fundamental: India is turning back to palm after China's cheap soyoil exports cooled, a modest demand offset to China halting palm purchases. It does not change the picture of Malaysian stocks well above average, and weaker crude still narrows the biodiesel pull.
events: China soyoil export boom cools as India turns to palm (Bloomberg)
China halts palm oil purchases as storage fills (Bloomberg)

natgas.fundamental: Jan eased about 1.5% to ~3.61 ahead of the holiday-shifted storage report, with a Texas chill offset by fading Northeast cash. Longer-dated support is building from LNG: reports see the global LNG supply crunch running into 2027 and data-centre gas demand rising.
events: Global LNG supply crunch set to spill into 2027 (OilPrice.com)
Goldman sees data-centre-driven gas demand surge (OilPrice.com)
Northeast cash rally fizzles as chill lifts Texas (Natural Gas Intelligence)

crude.fundamental: WTI Jan is steady near 82 after swinging overnight: supply-surplus worries and a small US crude stock build weigh, while Hormuz threats and China buying the dip support. OPEC+ is holding output; nothing has changed the surplus outlook.
events: Oil falls as traders weigh supply outlook and Mideast tensions (WSJ)
China goes on oil buying spree as prices slide (OilPrice.com)
US crude inventories inch up (OilPrice.com)

ulsd.fundamental: Distillate stocks remain below average, keeping cracks wide even as crude falls; Red Sea/Houthi risk is the main upside driver for diesel.
events: Oil falls on supply outlook and shipping risks (WSJ)
Dangote refinery IPO plan approved (Reuters)

rbob.fundamental: RBOB Jan eased to ~2.43 (-0.6%) with gasoline stocks holding steady and above average; the low-demand season keeps the margin story weak.
events: US crude stocks edge up, gasoline steady (OilPrice.com)
RBOB Jan ~2.43, -0.6% (NYMEX/Yahoo Finance)
